cognate: *dyew- 'sky, Sky-god' + *ph₂tér 'father': Ved. dyaúṣ/dyaùḥ pitā́/pítar ~ Gk Ζεῦ/Ζεὺς πάτερ/πατήρ ~ Lat. Iuppiter, Diespiter
drift_or_renewal: none in the core pair; Latin has fused it into one compound name (Iuppiter, Diespiter)
shared_syntax: theonym + appositive kinship noun 'father' naming the sky god. The slab's Vedic anchors give it as nominative predication (dyauś ca naḥ pitā, with pṛthivī ca mātā; dyaur naḥ pitā janitā); the Greek anchors give it as line-initial vocative of prayer (Ζεῦ πάτερ). The exact vocative match is in the support: RV 6.51.5 dyaùḥ pítar, AVŚ 6.4.6 dyauṣ pitar.
context: invocation of the sky god as father: AVP 5.21.1 calls on Sky-father, Earth-mother and Agni against fever ('dyauś ... pitā'); in the Greek anchors gods and men open prayers or speeches with 'Ζεῦ πάτερ'
phrase: *dyew- ph₂tér 'Father Sky' (Ved. dyauṣ pitā / dyauṣ pitar ~ Gk Ζεῦ πάτερ)

cognate: *médʰu 'mead, honey' + *swéh₂du- 'sweet': Gk μέθυ ἡδύ ~ Ved. svādú- ... mádhu- ~ OE swēte medu (Finn. 39 swētne medo)
drift_or_renewal: drift of the noun: Gk μέθυ = (sweet) wine, Ved. mádhu = honey / honeyed soma drink, OE medu = mead; the adjective is the same *sweh₂d- formation in all three
shared_syntax: Greek and OE give adjective + noun in one NP (μέθυ ἡδύ, line-end formula; swētne medo, acc.). In the slab's Vedic anchor svādu and madhu are coordinate predicates of annam ('let him make this food sweet, honey'), not a single NP; the RV support shows the pair as an NP or apposition (svādóḥ ... mádhvaḥ RV 1.84.10; svā́do pito mádho pito RV 1.187.2)
context: food and drink at a meal: AVP 5.28.8 asks that the gift-food be made sweet and honeyed; Od. 17.533 and the Telegonia line pair bread or meat with 'sweet drink' as the meal ('σῖτος καὶ μέθυ ἡδύ', 'κρέα ... καὶ μέθυ ἡδύ'); RV 1.187 praises Food (pitu) as 'sweet' and 'honeyed'; Finnsburg uses 'sweet mead' for the hall-feast

support.corpus: Greek poetry and prose to 300 BC (GLAUx 0020-001)

cognate: *deh₃- 'give' (agent noun *deh₃-tor-/-ter-, root noun -dā-) + *h₁wésu- 'good(s)': Gk δώτωρ/δωτήρ ἑάων ~ Ved. dātā́ vásūnām, vasu-dā́-, vásu-dāvan-
drift_or_renewal: the Greek agent noun is fully cognate (δώτωρ ~ dātár-); ἐύς survives in Greek almost only in this genitive-plural formula ('of goods'), so the phrase keeps an otherwise lost noun use. In the slab's Vedic anchors 'giver' is the root compound vasu-dā́ḥ (AVŚ 12.1.44) or is renewed as vasu-pati 'lord of goods' + vasūni sāviṣat (AVP 19.1.5); the agent-noun form dātā́ vásūnām is in RV 8.51.5
shared_syntax: agent noun 'giver' + genitive plural 'of goods' (or a compound of the same), used as an epithet of a deity, including in the vocative (δῶτορ ἑάων Od. 8.335 ~ vásudāvan RV 2.6.4)
context: cult epithet of gods as givers of wealth: Hermes addressed as 'δῶτορ ἑάων'; gods as 'δωτῆρες ἑάων' (Od. 8.325, Hesiod); Earth as 'vasu-dāḥ devī' who should give 'vasūni' (AVŚ 12.1.44); Savitṛ as 'vasupatiḥ' bringing 'vasūni' (AVP 19.1.5); Indra as 'dātā́ vásūnām'
phrase: *deh₃tōr h₁wesuHoHom 'giver of goods' (δωτῆρες ἑάων ~ dātā́ vásūnām)

note: 3 claims (2 high, 1 medium). Considered and dropped: κλέος εὐρύ (Od. 23.137, B-d903a; no Indic slab anchor with uru/pṛthu śravas), pṛthivī ... bhayante ~ folde bifode (B-7317f; mountains, not earth, are the subject of bhayante; biblical earthquake motif), Dieva dēls ~ Διὸς υἱός (B-79f96/B-cd37d; the Greek anchors are Hermes, contexts don't match), ugrā vaḥ santu bāhavaḥ (Indic only). Most bundles pair AV mantras with Greek or Latin prose and hold nothing inherited.
